rows: Start with useState for local values
A value only one component reads belongs in that component's own state, not in a store.
Keep the value next to the component that shows it.
Reach for a global store for a toggle or an input.
A value computed from props or state needs no state of its own; storing it creates two truths that drift.
Compute total, filtered list or label in the render body.
Mirror a derived value into state with an effect.
const total = items.reduce((sum, it) => sum + it.price * it.qty, 0)
Lift state to the nearest shared parent
Two siblings that must agree should read one value owned by their closest common parent.
Pass the value and its setter down as props.
Keep copies in both siblings and sync them.
Use a reducer when updates share rules
Several fields that change together, or many update paths, are easier to follow as named actions.
Use useReducer with action names that read as events.
Call five setters in a row to express one change.
State updates are queued; a function form reads the latest queued value.
Pass an updater when the next value depends on the last.
Read the variable from the render and set it twice.
React compares by identity; changing an object in place can leave the screen stale.
Create a new object or array and set it.
Push into an array held in state.
Reset a subtree with a key
A different key makes React discard the old component state and start fresh.
Key a form or profile panel by the record id.
Write an effect that clears each field when the id changes.
Keep state structure flat and free of duplicates
Nested copies of the same record must be updated in several places.
Store ids in one place and look the record up.
Hold the selected object and the list it came from.
Use context for rarely changing shared values
Theme, locale and the signed-in user fit context; fast-changing values re-render every consumer.
Split contexts by how often they change.
Put a typing buffer in a context everyone reads.
Provide context as a component in 19
React 19 lets the context object render as its own provider.
Write the context directly as the wrapper.
Effects are for syncing with outside systems
Subscriptions, timers, and non-React widgets need an effect; reacting to a click does not.
Do event work in the event handler.
Run a post request from an effect after a click flag flips.
Always return a cleanup for subscriptions
Without cleanup, listeners and timers pile up across re-renders and in StrictMode's double run.
Return a function that undoes what the effect set up.
Add a listener and leave it attached.
List every reactive value in the dependency array
An omitted dependency makes the effect read stale values.
Fix the code so the lint rule is quiet.
Fetch with a guard against stale responses
A slow earlier response can land after a newer one.
Set an ignore flag in cleanup, or use a framework data layer.
Set state from whichever response arrives last.
It keeps a store subscription consistent during concurrent rendering.
Subscribe through the hook for browser or store state.
Copy store values into state inside an effect.
Use useLayoutEffect only for measuring before paint
It blocks the browser from painting; most effects do not need that.
Measure a tooltip then place it, in a layout effect.
Use refs for values that do not drive the screen
Timer ids and DOM nodes live in a ref; changing a ref does not re-render.
Store ids and instances in useRef.
Use a ref callback for node setup and teardown
In 19 a ref callback can return a cleanup function.
Return a cleanup from the callback.
Attach observers in an effect that queries the DOM by id.
Pass ref as a prop in 19
Function components receive ref as a normal prop, so forwardRef is no longer needed for new code.
Same props and state must give the same output, with no writes to outside values.
Mutate a module variable or call Math.random for output.
Use stable keys from the data
Keys tell React which row is which; index keys break state when rows reorder.
Use array index for a list that can change.
A component defined inside another is a new type every render and loses its state.
Declare components at the top level.
Declare a component inside a render body.
A bare number on the left of && prints on the page.
Return fragments instead of wrapper divs
Extra wrappers break table, list and grid markup.
Use <>...</> when no element is needed.
Wrap rows in a div inside a table.
It double-runs renders and effects to expose impure code and missing cleanup.
Keep StrictMode around the app root.
Remove it to hide a double-fire.
memo, useMemo and useCallback have a cost and help only where renders are slow.
Profile first, then memoize the hot spot.
Try the React Compiler before hand-memoizing
The compiler memoizes automatically when code follows the rules of React.
Enable the compiler and delete redundant memo calls.
Hand-memoize everything in a compiler project.
Keep state close to where it is used
State high in the tree re-renders everything below it on each keystroke.
Move fast-changing state into a small child.
Store input text at the app root.
<App> holds q for the whole page
Split code with lazy and Suspense
Routes and heavy widgets need not ship in the first bundle.
Import a charting library on the landing page.
The input stays responsive while an expensive list catches up.
Defer the query that feeds the heavy list.
startTransition keeps clicks and typing responsive while a tab or route switch renders.
Block the UI with a long synchronous render.
Thousands of DOM nodes cost memory and layout time.
React DOM exposes preload and preconnect calls for fonts, scripts and images.
Call preload for the hero image or font.
Wait for CSS to discover a late font.
A function passed to action receives FormData and works with pending state.
Pass a function to the form's action.
Write onSubmit with preventDefault for every form.
A submit button inside the form can read whether it is sending.
Disable the button and name the action while pending.
The state returned from the action feeds messages back to the form.
Return an errors object from the action.
Show the expected result at once and fall back if the request fails.
Add the pending item to the list instantly.
Make the user wait for the round trip.
Placeholder text vanishes and is not a name for assistive tech (WCAG 2.2 SC 1.3.1, 3.3.2).
Use a label tied with htmlFor and useId.
Use the right input type and autocomplete
Correct type and autocomplete tokens bring the right keyboard and autofill (WCAG 2.2 SC 1.3.5).
Switching an input between controlled and uncontrolled logs warnings and loses values.
Start with undefined then set a value.
Tell people about errors in text
Colour alone is not enough (SC 1.4.1); announce errors near the field (SC 3.3.1).
Link the message with aria-describedby and set aria-invalid.
Booking form: keep one clear primary action
A booking or quote form converts when the fields are few and the button names the result.
Ask name, phone, time; label the button Book a visit.
Add ten optional fields and a button labelled Submit.
button, a, nav, main and headings carry roles and keyboard behaviour for free (SC 4.1.2).
Use button for actions and a for navigation.
Focus must be visible (SC 2.4.7) and move sensibly after route or dialog changes.
Move focus to the dialog or page heading with a ref.
A tel link works for keyboard, screen readers and phones.
Render an a element with tel: and the number as its text.
Use a button that sets window.location.
Informative images need alt (SC 1.1.1); decoration gets empty alt.
Write alt that says what the image shows.
Users who ask for less motion should not get parallax or large slides (SC 2.3.3).
Read the media query and skip the animation.
Set the page title per view
Render <title> in the component; React hoists it.
Leave one static title for every route.
WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 asks for 24 by 24 CSS pixels at least; 44 is friendlier.
Use portals for dialogs but keep order
createPortal renders outside the parent DOM; focus trap and labelling remain your job.
Label the dialog and return focus on close.
Read promises with use and Suspense
use unwraps a promise passed from a server component, with Suspense for the wait.
Pass the promise and wrap in Suspense.
Create the promise during client render.
Boundaries let parts of the page appear as they load.
Wrap slow sections with a skeleton fallback.
Block the whole page on one fetch.
Catch render errors with a boundary
An uncaught render error unmounts the tree; a boundary shows a fallback.
Wrap risky sections in an error boundary.
Leave a blank page on failure.
In server components cache avoids repeating the same read in one request.
Fetch the same row in five components.
Only files that need state, effects or events need use client.
Put use client at the top of the layout.
Treat server functions as public endpoints
A use server function can be called by any client; check auth and validate input inside it.
Verify the session and parse input.
async function pay(fd){'use server'; await requireUser(); ...}
Keep secrets and tokens off the client
Anything in a client bundle is readable.
Read secrets only in server code.
Put a secret key in a VITE_ or NEXT_PUBLIC_ variable.
A hidden button is not access control.
Check the session on the server for every protected read and write.
Only hide links when logged out.
Stripe Checkout: create the session on the server
A hosted checkout page keeps card data off your site; the price comes from your server.
Create the session server-side and redirect to its url.
Send the amount from the browser.
The success redirect can be skipped or faked; fulfil from a signed event.
Verify the signature and fulfil on checkout.session.completed.
Mark an order paid on the success page load.
Keep components idempotent for strict double renders
Rendering twice must give the same result, or StrictMode reveals the bug.
Move side effects to handlers and effects.
React 19 hoists title, meta and link tags into the head.
Place meta tags inside the page component.
The precedence prop lets React order and dedupe stylesheets and wait before reveal.
Add href and precedence to link.
Inject style tags after first paint.
Avoid server and client output mismatches
Dates, random ids and window checks that differ between server and client break hydration.
Render stable values; do browser-only work after mount.
Call Date.now() or window.innerWidth in render.
useId gives the same id on server and client.
Use it for label and aria links.
Give images dimensions and lazy loading
Width and height prevent layout shift (CLS); lazy loading saves bytes.
Set width, height, loading='lazy' below the fold.
Ship the hero as lazy; omit size.
The largest image above the fold should not be lazy and can be preloaded.
Use fetchPriority high on the one hero.
Composing with children avoids a prop for every variation.
Add boolean props for every layout variant.
Do not copy props into state
A prop copied into initial state ignores later updates.
Use the prop directly, or reset with a key.
Initialise state from a prop that will change.
If a parent must call focus or scroll, expose just those methods.
Hand the entire DOM node to the parent.
